expectations.name: tpm2_session_command_authentication
expectations.intent: Every TPM command sent with an HMAC session must be authenticated: the TPM must receive the same command parameters, handles, nonces, and attributes that the host intended, and the HMAC must be computed over the correct cpHash.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_response_authentication
expectations.intent: Every TPM response received with an HMAC session must be authenticated: the host must verify that the response parameters, return code, nonces, and attributes match the HMAC computed by the TPM.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_command_payload_confidentiality
expectations.intent: The first command parameter encrypted with AES-CFB under the session key must remain confidential from an attacker who observes the TPM transport.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_response_payload_confidentiality
expectations.intent: The response parameter encrypted with AES-CFB under the session key must remain confidential from an attacker who observes the TPM transport.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_key_secrecy
expectations.intent: The session key (sessionKey) derived from the salt and nonces must remain secret from an attacker who observes the TPM transport.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_salt_secrecy
expectations.intent: The session salt (sessionSalt) derived from the ECDH shared secret must remain secret from an attacker who observes the TPM transport.

expectations.name: tpm2_null_key_public_material_validation
expectations.intent: The host must validate that the public key material (x, y coordinates) returned by the TPM in the CreatePrimary response matches the expected template for a NULL key (ECC P-256, specific attributes).

expectations.name: tpm2_initial_create_primary_mitm_attack
expectations.intent: The initial TPM2_CreatePrimary command is not session protected, so an attacker can perform a Man-in-the-Middle attack to return a public key they control, allowing interception and decoding of all subsequent session-based transactions.

expectations.name: tpm2_continued_session_state_reset
expectations.intent: When a session is continued (TPM2_SA_CONTINUE_SESSION attribute set), the auth->session offset must be reset to TPM_HEADER_SIZE for the next command, and the session key and nonces must remain unchanged.

expectations.name: tpm2_session_termination_cleanup
expectations.intent: When a session is terminated (TPM2_SA_CONTINUE_SESSION not set), the session context must be flushed and the auth structure must be freed to prevent resource leaks.
